questions.question: What MUST happen when materials arrive at intake?
questions.explanation: Materials must be checked before booking in, against the agreed specification.

questions.question: How are foreign body hazards controlled?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes approved knives, blade checks and intact equipment to control foreign bodies. Of the options, using equipment is the closest fit; it does not state this answer explicitly.

questions.question: What is carried out after equipment has been repaired or maintained by engineering?
questions.explanation: Cleaning controls contamination and removes debris. The booklet does not explicitly describe the step immediately after engineering work, so cleaning is the likely intended answer.

questions.question: Why are the physical characteristics of a product checked?
options: To enable customer to recognise it when buying
To ensure that product can be made correctly
questions.explanation: Receipt checks ensure materials match the agreed specification, and processing checks confirm that the product is as it should be.

questions.question: What is the BEST course of action taken to take if you see a full waste bin?
questions.explanation: Clean As You Go and the waste guidance require tidying and preventing waste from piling up. Emptying the bin is the likely intended option, though the booklet does not specify the response to a full bin.

questions.question: What is material authenticity?
options: Material that is what it says it is
Material that is kind to the planet
questions.explanation: The booklet requires evidence for claims about materials and conformity to specification. Authenticity is not explicitly defined; the first option is the likely intended definition.

questions.question: Why is it important to have security in place?
options: To prevent deliberate or malicious contamination of the product
To maintain order on site for incoming traffic
To keep employees on site safe from harm
questions.explanation: Site access is controlled to protect against contamination. Deliberate or malicious contamination is not explicitly discussed, so the first option is a best-fit inference.

questions.question: What needs the MOST protection on site from pests?
questions.explanation: Pests can damage or contaminate the product; closed doors and tidy waste areas help prevent entry and infestation.

questions.question: What impact does unclean equipment have when microbes are left behind?
options: Swabs cannot be used for testing
questions.explanation: Unclean equipment can introduce microbes, and contamination can make consumers sick. Complaints are a likely consequence.

questions.question: What must you do if your spectacles are broken during working hours?
options: Report the breakage to your supervisor immediately
Report the breakage to your supervisor after break
Report the breakage to your supervisor before leaving site
questions.explanation: Breakages must be reported to the supervisor immediately to protect product and materials.

questions.question: Why is waste put into separate storage bins?
options: It’ cleaned and collected on different days
There are different uses for waste materials
All waste must be recycled correctly
questions.explanation: The waste section requires proper disposal, labelled bins and closed outside containers, but gives no reason for separating waste. It cannot resolve the choice between different uses and correct recycling.

questions.question: What happens when glass breakage occurs?
options: The cleaning of the area is delayed
questions.explanation: Surrounding product and materials must be checked for glass contamination, and unsafe product must be held under corrective-action procedures. Holding product is the likely answer, but the booklet does not explicitly say that every glass breakage automatically triggers a hold.

questions.question: What information does the weight of material delivery provides?
questions.explanation: The amount of material received is recorded for traceability.

questions.question: Why does clean equipment need to be kept clean after it’s washed?
options: So, it doesn’t’ contaminate the product
So, it can be tested before it’s used again
So that it is checked for damage
questions.explanation: Cleaning controls contamination, and cleaning equipment must itself be kept clean.

questions.question: How do fabric conveyors contaminate the product?
options: The product of them is not correctly spaced out
Frayed pieces can fall off them and get into the product
Too much product on them makes them unsafe
questions.explanation: Broken equipment parts can fall into product. The same principle supports frayed conveyor pieces, although fabric conveyors are not specifically mentioned.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a key principle of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) in food safety?
options: Using only organic ingredients in all products
Ensuring that all employees wash their hands before handling food
Labelling food products with promotional offers
questions.explanation: Handwashing removes microbes and is required before entering processing and handling areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a personal hygiene requirement under GMP?
questions.explanation: PPE protects personnel and the product and is included under contamination controls.

questions.question: Which of the following practices violates GMP?
questions.explanation: Equipment must be intact and checked for damage; damage or malfunction must be reported immediately.

questions.question: If you have a cut or sore, what should you do?
options: Cover it will company issue blue plaster
Cover it with skin coloured plaster
Sign out of work and go home
questions.explanation: Only site-issued blue plasters are allowed.

questions.question: Which information is essential for food traceability?
options: Batch or lot number, supplier, and destination
questions.explanation: Traceability covers materials from delivery through processing, storage and dispatch; supplier batch or lot codes are recorded at intake.
